paragraphs.text: Pin workspaces whose sessions are running or waiting for your reply to the top of the DSH sidebar.
# @lixiangzhong/dsh-active-chat

Pins **workspaces with in-progress sessions** to the top of the DSH sidebar, so you can
always see w
hich chats are actually working.

The DSH sidebar keeps a single Host workspace order that only changes by dragging. This
plugin write

s that order automatically whenever a workspace becomes active: its workspace
moves to the front, an

d the rest follow below in their previous relative order. When the
work finishes, the workspace sink

s back below the still-active ones — it is not restored
to its old manual slot.

"In progress" is the same signal the sidebar's own activity dot uses: a session that is
running, or
a session that is waiting for your reply (approval / plan review / question).
## Behaviour

- **Boot / first install** — aligns once. The workspace that became active most recently
goes first;

every other workspace keeps its current relative order. If the sidebar is
already aligned, nothing

is written.
- **New activation** — the workspace jumps to the top. If several workspaces are active,

the most recently activated one is the highest.
- **Work finishes** — the workspace sinks below the

workspaces that are still active.
- **Everything idle** — the plugin stops writing. Your manual dra

disable or uninstall the plugin to
turn it off.

The order written by the plugin is the real Host workspace order (the same one a manual
drag produce
s), so it persists across reloads and other sessions.

## How it works

`client.js` is a browser-side plugin. It injects the `workspaces`, `sessions` and
`uiSession` client

services, subscribes to their snapshots, and calls the documented
`ctx.workspaces.insertBefore(work

spaceId, beforeWorkspaceId?)` service to move a workspace
within the Host order. Changes are coalesc

ed and only written when the set of active
workspaces actually changes. The Host half (`index.js`) i
s an empty plugin entry.

## Releasing
Publishing runs in CI; this repository stores no npm token.

1. Bump the version and let npm write the release commit and tag: `npm version 0.1.1`
(add `--no-git

-tag-version` if you prefer to write the commit and tag yourself).
2. Push both: `git push origin ma

ster` and `git push origin v0.1.1`
(or `git push --follow-tags`). The `v*` tag starts the release wo

rkflow.
3. `.github/workflows/publish.yml` checks that the tag
matches `package.json`, runs `npm tes

t`, and publishes through
npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC), which
also attaches a provenance attestatio

, and publishes through
npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC), which
also attaches a provenance attestation.

Prerequisite: the npm package must list `.github/workflows/publish.yml` as a trusted
publisher (user

`lixiangzhong`, repository `dsh-active-chat`) with **Allow npm publish**
enabled — new configuratio

ns default to stage-only publishing. A trusted-publisher
configuration expires unless its first succ

essful publish happens within two days of
creation.
